answer.generated: Real-time databases must prioritize predictable response times over data consistency, as unpredictable delays from disk access make main-memory databases essential for meeting strict deadlines. Even in memory, lock waits and transaction aborts introduce variability, necessitating concurrency control strategies like extended locking or optimistic protocols to minimize missed deadlines. This focus contrasts with non-real-time databases, where consistency is prioritized even at the cost of occasional delays.
